_comment: CurriculumOS V1 genesis seed. Curated foundational concepts from open educational resources (OpenStax). Each kernel's anchored quotes are verified by the foundry's mechanical anchor check against the sourceSnapshots below before admission. Scaling to the full ~50-title library is the next foundry run.

sourceSnapshots.openstax:microeconomics-3e#5: Price elasticity of demand measures the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price; it is computed as the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in price. Demand is described as elastic when the absolute value of the elasticity is greater than one, meaning quantity responds proportionally more than price. Demand is inelastic when the absolute value is less than one. Necessities tend to have inelastic demand because consumers have few substitutes, while luxuries tend to have elastic demand. The availability of close substitutes is a primary determinant of elasticity.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:microeconomics-3e#3: A demand curve shows the quantity of a good that consumers are willing and able to purchase at each price, holding all other factors constant. Demand curves typically slope downward, reflecting the law of demand: as price falls, quantity demanded rises. A change in price causes a movement along the demand curve, whereas a change in income, tastes, or the price of related goods shifts the entire curve.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:statistics#7: A sampling distribution is the probability distribution of a statistic obtained from a large number of samples drawn from a specific population. The central limit theorem states that the sampling distribution of the sample mean approaches a normal distribution as the sample size increases, regardless of the shape of the population distribution. The standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the mean is the population standard deviation divided by the square root of the sample size.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:statistics#9: A p-value is the probability of obtaining a test statistic at least as extreme as the one observed, assuming the null hypothesis is true. A small p-value indicates that the observed data would be unlikely under the null hypothesis. The p-value is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true, and it does not measure the size of an effect.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:biology-2e#8: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose. The light-dependent reactions capture energy from sunlight to produce ATP and NADPH, which the Calvin cycle then uses to fix carbon dioxide into sugar. Oxygen is released as a byproduct of splitting water molecules.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:biology-2e#3: The cell membrane, also called the plasma membrane, is a selectively permeable barrier that regulates which substances enter and leave the cell. It is composed of a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins. The membrane maintains the internal environment of the cell while allowing the exchange of nutrients and wastes.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:chemistry-2e#13: Chemical equilibrium is the state in which the forward and reverse reaction rates are equal, so the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant over time. Equilibrium is dynamic: both the forward and reverse reactions continue to occur even though no net change is observed. According to Le Chatelier's principle, when a system at equilibrium is disturbed by a change in concentration, temperature, or pressure, the equilibrium shifts in the direction that partially counteracts the disturbance.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:microeconomics-3e#4: Market equilibrium occurs at the price where the quantity demanded by buyers equals the quantity supplied by sellers. At this equilibrium price the opposing pressures of demand and supply are balanced and there is no tendency for the price to change. When the price is above equilibrium a surplus pushes it down, and when the price is below equilibrium a shortage pushes it up, so the market mechanism restores the balance.
